text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-AHRAM

- President Hosni Mubarak said in an interview with state television that measures were being taken quietly for the sake of Jerusalem and that the United States was looking for a formula for the return of all Syrian territory.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri said Mubarak's foreign trip achieved positive results for the economy and attracting investment. A fund will be set up to protect the country from dumping, subsidies and sudden increases in imports.
- Supply and Trade Minister Ahmed Gueily told the Shoura Council that the government was about to complete a plan to help the spinning and weaving industry.
- The International Monetary Fund (IMF) representative in Cairo, Arvind Subramanian, told the state news agency MENA that Egypt would receive $1.3 billion in foreign capital this year.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said Israeli practices were weakening confidence in the peace process.
- The Interior Ministry has completed its preparations for local elections. The Counmcil of State ruled that those newly registered this year do not have the right to vote or to stand as candidates.

- An official source in the prime minister's office said that the new investment law does not mean that the General Organisation for Investment is being abolished but that it will have a new role promoting investment projects.
AL-AKHBAR

- Mubarak, in television interview, said his message to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was that peace is worth concessions. He said that Arab measures were being taken quietly on Jerusalem.
- It has been decided to allocate one billion pounds ($290 million) as soft loans to farmers to cover the costs of summer crops such as cotton and rice.
- A front-page editorial says that attacks on Israelis are the natural outcome of the Israeli government's policies.
- The Supreme Constitutional Court ruled that it could no longer be considered a crime to demand "key money" as a condition for letting real estate.
- Fifteen people drowned when a minibus went off the road near Beni Suef and fell into an irrigation canal.
AL-GOMHURIA
- Mubarak says that the existence of differences between Egypt and the United States does not mean there is a crisis.
- Chief of Staff Magdi Hettata starts a visit to Turkey today. He will meet the president and defence minister.
$1 = 3.395 pounds
